analysis: The PR splits release-swift.yml into a thin trigger router and a new reusable release-provider.yml. The reusable workflow holds the sign, notarize, stage, and publish chain. It is called once per lane (dev, staging, prod) with `secrets: inherit`. Master pushes now also start a staging lane, gated by vars.STAGING_ENABLED. All lanes sign with the same Developer ID. A comment says resolve-provider-release.sh refuses prod on non-tag triggers. That script and the prod job's `if` condition are not in the supplied units, because the patch is truncated, so that tag-gating of the prod signing identity is unverified. Visible controls look preserved: the signed artifact is downloaded by artifact id and digest; the final post-notarization smoke checks run on the extracted archive; and the full CodeDirectory SHA-256 is extracted from the final signed provider binary and recorded in the publication identity. Publication and registration happen in a separate job, `publish-release`, with a per-environment concurrency group. Secret scoping uses `environment == 'prod' && secrets.PROD_*` expressions; DEV_* secrets are passed to every lane, which is existing behavior. The finding is the unpinned pip install of awscli in jobs where RELEASE_KEY and R2 credentials are already in GITHUB_ENV (lines 1059 and 1174). The integration pass should check these in the unseen parts: the first 570 lines of release-provider.yml, scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh, and whether a staging lane on a push resolves to environment=staging rather than dev. They should also check whether the removed top-level concurrency lets prod runs overlap, and whether the 'already signed' guard and the resume paths still hold per lane.

findings.detail: In publish-release, the 'Resolve env-specific secrets' step appends r2_secret_access_key, release_key and coordinator_url to $GITHUB_ENV (lines 1140-1155). The next steps then run `pip install awscli` into a fresh venv with no version or hash pinning (line 1174). The same pattern appears in stage-release at line 1059, where R2 keys are exported. Every GitHub Action in this workflow is pinned by SHA, but this PyPI install is not. A compromised or typosquatted awscli or dependency release would execute with RELEASE_KEY and R2 write keys in its environment. The attacker could then register a malicious binary hash with the coordinator (A-005, A-011), overwrite release objects in R2, or publish aliases. The base-side workflow is not visible in the supplied patch, so I cannot tell whether this install is new. Fix: install from a hash-pinned requirements file with `--require-hashes`, or use a pinned preinstalled CLI. Also install the tools before secrets are exported to GITHUB_ENV, and pass secrets only to the single step that needs them.
findings.title: Unpinned `pip install awscli` runs in publish job after release key and R2 credentials are exported
